# Safety classes {#safety-classes}

Every tool in the catalogue carries a safety classification in the
manifest. The classification decides how the tool is surfaced — what
runs by default, what asks first, what stays behind an explicit
opt-in.

| Class | Meaning | Default posture |
|---|---|---|
| `safe` | self-contained; no live firing | installable and runnable normally |
| `requires-target` | fires requests at a target system | runs only when given an explicit target |
| `exp` | experimental code execution surface | gated behind the lab-mode wrapper contract; opt-in |

The default-off posture is a design decision, recorded as an
architecture decision record in the OS repository: tools in the
`exp` class never become reachable through menu or CLI defaults.
Safety class surfaces on every generated reference page, and the
wrapper contract for `exp` tools is emitted by the same generator that
builds the category modules.
